key_insight: The paper proposes physics-informed neural plasticity, where a PDE solver changes its internal representation during training to shift capacity toward regions with unresolved physics.
engineering_relevance: This could make physics-informed solvers more accurate and efficient on heterogeneous PDEs by automatically allocating model capacity where the solution is hardest to learn.
method: ReCAP uses Gaussian-localized components with adaptive local enrichment.
It refines the representation via residual-directed splitting, gate-based pruning, and function-aware merging.
Quiet-child refinement initializes new components to minimize disruption during splitting.
evidence_signal: Across five challenging 3D and 4D PDE benchmarks against 11 competing physics-informed solvers, ReCAP achieved the lowest relative L2 error on every problem, improving by 10.7%–27.5% over the strongest baseline.
watch_item: The adaptive splitting/merging logic and stability guarantees may add implementation complexity and require careful tuning of residual indicators and refinement thresholds.
paper_title: Physics-Informed Neural Plasticity: PDE Solvers That Reshape Themselves
